  "leave_information": [
    [
      "Vacation days: The employee is entitled to 180 vacation hours per year with retention of salary (for the calculation of the number of vacation days per year, 7.2 hours per day is assumed). The salary for the application of this article refers to the wage as defined in Article 7:610 in conjunction with 7:639 of the Dutch Civil Code. As of 1 January 2023, the accrual of age-related vacation hours ceases. If and insofar as an employee is entitled to more than the number of vacation hours mentioned in paragraph 1 on 31 December 2022, the employee retains this higher number of vacation hours per year. The employee will not receive a higher number of vacation hours per year upon reaching the age of 55 or older after 31 December 2022. The calculation of vacation hours accrual is pro-rata to the exact date of commencement or termination of employment in any year. Vacation hours (with the exception of vacation hours exceeding the minimum referred to in Article 7:634 of the Dutch Civil Code) must be taken within six months after the last day of the calendar year in which the entitlement was acquired. Vacation hours exceeding the minimum referred to in Article 7:634 of the Dutch Civil Code expire five years after the last day of the calendar year in which the entitlement was acquired. In deviation from paragraph 5, it can be mutually agreed that vacation hours not exceeding the minimum referred to in Article 7:634 of the Dutch Civil Code can also be taken after the expiry period of six months. The employee, who due to circumstances beyond their control is reasonably unable to take all or part of their due vacation hours, will be given the opportunity to take them at a later time to be determined in consultation with the employer. The employee has the right to take at least 21 consecutive days of vacation once a year to prevent being scheduled on the Saturday preceding the vacation. Furthermore, the employee's wishes regarding the scheduling of work immediately following the vacation will be taken into account. The start and end times of the vacation are determined by the employer, in accordance with the employee's wishes, unless serious reasons oppose it. The employee will generally submit the leave request in writing at least two weeks in advance. If the employer does not provide the employee with the serious reasons in writing within two weeks after the employee has communicated their wishes in writing to the employer, the vacation is set in accordance with the employee's wishes. The provisions in this article apply as a minimum regulation, from which the employer is free to deviate upwards in favor of the employee."

An employee can never perform more than 45 hours of work in a week. An employee can be scheduled for a maximum of 9 extra hours per week in addition to their appointment size.       "Overtime definition: Overtime is defined as work that is incidentally performed beyond the scheduled working hours, where the exceeding of the normal annual working hours is measured. Until 1 January 2023, overtime was defined as work that is incidentally performed beyond the scheduled working hours, where the exceeding of the average contractual working hours on an annual basis was measured. If the work immediately follows the employee's usual working time or performed shift and is shorter than fifteen minutes, this working time up to a maximum of fifteen minutes is not eligible for compensation. The aforementioned period of fifteen minutes of overtime can only occur incidentally. Daytime work, whether or not combined with evening work, including overtime, lasts a maximum of 11 hours. Night work, including overtime, lasts a maximum of 10 hours."

    [
      "Overtime compensation: Compensation for overtime is provided in the form of free time, equal to the number of hours the overtime lasted, in compliance with Article 15 paragraph 2 of the CAO. Overtime is generally compensated in the same calendar year; if this is not possible, then no later than 1 July of the year following the calendar year in which the overtime occurred. The aforementioned free time is taken in consultation between the employer and employee. If no agreement is reached on taking the free time, the employer has the decisive vote, taking into account the employee's wishes as much as possible. If overtime cannot be compensated in free time within the aforementioned periods, it will be compensated financially. Overtime will then be compensated per hour with a supplement of 25% on the hourly wage. At the employee's request, accumulated hours, up to a maximum of 72 hours, can be carried over as compensable overtime into the period after 1 July of the year following the year in which the hours accrued. These hours are booked with a factor of 1.25, so a maximum of 90 compensation hours can be carried over. Any hours exceeding 72 that have not been compensated by 1 July of the year following the year in which the hours accrued must be paid out in accordance with paragraph 4. In deviation from the foregoing, the employer and employee may agree to pay out overtime hours in money earlier than 1 July following the calendar year in which the overtime hours accrued. This payment can take place at the end of the calendar year in which the overtime occurred or at any time in the first half of the following calendar year. This earlier payment in money can only take place by mutual agreement between and with the consent of the employer and employee."

    [
      "On-call duty (General Pharmacy): On-call duty is defined as a period between two consecutive shifts or during a break, during which the employee is obliged to be reachable in their free time to perform work as soon as possible in unforeseen circumstances. An on-call duty can only be assigned if the nature of the work makes it necessary and if it cannot reasonably be prevented by organizing the work in another way. On-call duty is exclusively intended for times when few or virtually no care requests are expected. If an on-call duty is performed, the employee spends a maximum of 13 hours on handling care requests per 24-hour period. The aforementioned maximum applies, including the shift immediately following the on-call duty. The maximum duration of the shift is observed. The employee performs on average a maximum of 45 hours of work per week in every 26-week period. All hours within an on-call duty – both work from call-outs and hours of mandatory presence – count as working time for determining the maximum permissible number of hours to be worked. In every 4-week period, the employee may be assigned on-call duty in two weeks. The employee may be assigned on-call duty a maximum of 3 times in any consecutive week. The employee may be assigned on-call duty a maximum of 26 times per quarter. The uninterrupted rest period before and after an on-call duty is at least 11 hours, which may be shortened once per week to at least 8 hours if, after such a shortening of the rest period has occurred, the subsequent uninterrupted rest period is at least 11 hours and is extended by at least the number of hours by which the preceding uninterrupted rest period was less than 11 hours (on-call duties of a maximum of 24 hours cannot be linked). Additionally, a week with on-call duties has at least one uninterrupted rest period of 24 hours. The compensation for on-call duty is 25% of the hourly wage per hour AND 1 hour of free time per care request. If 3 or more care requests occur during an on-call duty between 00:00 and 07:00 (until 1 January 2023: between 00:00 and 08:00), this duty is considered night work for rest periods, breaks, and compensation."

Criteria for dispensation: (a) temporary special circumstances, deviating from industry practice, making it unreasonable to fully apply the CAO; (b) an equivalent alternative arrangement agreed upon with an independent employee organization; (c) consent from the Works Council (OR), Personnel Representation (PVT), or personnel. Process: Vaste Commissie checks completeness within 2 weeks, employer can supplement within 2 weeks. Dispensation requires at least two-thirds agreement from both employer and employee representatives. It has no reduction in salary as a consequence."], ["Weekly working hours agreement", "The employee makes agreements with their employer about the 'working hours'. This is the number of hours to be worked per week. These working hours are laid down in the individual employment contract."], ["Full-time work week", "A full-time employment is 40 hours per week. This includes 38 working hours, and two free hours related to working time reduction (ATV). Unless contractually agreed otherwise, all within the standard regulations of the Working Hours Act."], ["Four-day work week", "Anyone who wishes can request a four-day work week. The employer may refuse such a request, but only if insurmountable problems would arise in terms of scheduling. The employer must be able to demonstrate these problems. If the employer and employee cannot reach an agreement, they can appeal to the Vaste Commissie."], ["Part-time work week", "There is a part-time employment if the employee is employed for less than 40 hours per week. If there is a part-time employment, the provisions of this CAO apply pro rata, unless otherwise specified in the relevant article."], ["Right to part-time work", "Anyone who wishes can become a part-timer. The employer may only refuse if it is demonstrably detrimental to the company for a specific function to be performed part-time."], ["Standard working hours", "Working hours are between 07:00 and 19:00. For employees participating in the hours bank, working hours are between 07:00 and 20:00."], ["Working hours per day", "The employee normally works no longer than eight hours per day."], ["Working hours per week", "The employee normally works no longer than 40 hours per week. If the employer deems it necessary, longer work weeks must be made. This is considered overtime, and it is compensated extra. The employee is never obliged to work more than five hours per week, or more than sixteen hours per period of four weeks. How the weekly working hours are distributed over the working days depends on the agreements in the employment contract. These agreements on working hours do not apply to sales representatives and managers authorized to assign overtime. If an employer changes working hours and/or schedules, the employer will do so in consultation with the employee. When establishing the schedule, the employer will take into account the personal circumstances and wishes of the employee as much as possible. If the employer cannot take into account the employee's wishes due to serious reasons based on compelling business interests, they must notify the employee in writing with arguments."], ["Employment contract details", "Upon employment, the employee receives a written employment contract containing: names and residences of parties; place(s) of work (or variable/free choice); employee's function and applicable function group; start date; duration (if fixed-term); vacation entitlement or other specified leave or calculation method; CAO applicability; salary scale and periodic, and payment method/frequency; duration and conditions of probation period (max 2 months for indefinite or >6 months fixed-term, not allowed for <=6 months fixed-term); pension scheme participation; weekly hours (full-time/part-time) and, if variable, guaranteed hours, pay for hours above guaranteed, and days/hours employee can be required to work; for temporary employment, identity of hiring company if known. If the use of hazardous substances is absolutely unavoidable, they must be stored under strict supervision and applied with great caution. They get the opportunity to work 60% (with a minimum of 2.5 days per week, 20 hours), while retaining 80% of their salary and 100% pension accrual."], ["Generation Pact general rules and conditions", "Upon participation in the Generation Pact, the surrendered gross wage is compensated by half by the employer. This creates opportunities for younger employees in the company, leading to gradual rejuvenation while retaining the experience of older employees (mentorship). Pension premium: Employer and employee pay the pension premium based on the original gross wage according to the applicable premium distribution. Senior days forfeited: If the Generation Pact is used, the right to so-called senior days (=extra vacation days for older employees, see article 6.2 of the CAO) is forfeited from the effective date. Additionally, the right to 6 of the 8 employability days (see article 7.2 of the CAO) is forfeited. By using the generation pact, you work part-time, and thus the right to ATV is forfeited, this is settled in the salary (article 5.4 CAO). Voluntary participation: Participation in the Generation Pact is not mandatory for the employee. It is therefore important that the employee and employer discuss the potential consequences well in advance of the desired start date (at least 3 months prior). Also, clarify what knowledge and skills can be transferred. Companies with 10 or fewer employees have, or may have, a compelling interest to reject a request for participation in the generation pact, provided they can substantiate this compelling interest. Eligibility: All employees aged 60 and older who work in the Tire and Wheel Industry and have been employed in the industry for at least 3 years immediately prior to the request for application of the generation pact (temporary contracts and temporary employment periods count towards the 3-year employment period) have the possibility to use the Generation Pact. This is only possible if the employee takes the initiative or agrees to participate (employee's choice). The request for application of the Generation Pact is not possible if, within 12 months prior to this request, the employee has invoked the Flexible Work Act and this request has also been (partially) honored. The employee can only 'switch' once from the 80/90/100 scheme to the 60/80/100 scheme and not vice versa. Once the employee has chosen to use the generation pact, this scheme can only be stopped with the employer's consent. If the generation pact applies, the employee can no longer invoke the Flexible Work Act, or rather, the Generation Pact constitutes a reason for the employer to reject such a request. Pension: If you participate in the generation pact, this does not affect the amount of your pension benefit. Both the employer and employee will continue to contribute to the pension fund based on the original gross wage and the applicable premium distribution. If you wish to use (partial) pension, any previously made agreements based on the generation pact will lapse. Sickness and disability: If you participate in the Generation Pact and are disabled for two years, you may receive a WIA benefit. This is based on the social insurance wage earned in the year prior to the first day of illness. Participation in the Generation Pact can therefore have consequences for this. Unemployment benefit: If you use the Generation Pact and become unemployed, this may affect your WW benefit. The unemployment benefit is linked to the social insurance wage. Because your actually earned wage decreases (90% or 80%) when participating in the Generation Pact, your social insurance wage also decreases, and with it the amount of any WW benefit. Any transition payment you may be entitled to will also be lower. Allowances: For the consequences of any government allowances, please visit www.toeslagen.nl. Disputes: In case of disputes, the Vaste Commissie can be consulted, see appendix 2 of the CAO. One-time switch from 80/90/100 scheme to 60/80/100 scheme: If the employee wishes to use the 60/80/100 variant and has already used option 1 (80/90/100 variant), the situation as it was prior to the generation pact is leading for the application of the various percentages. Example calculation provided for a switch from 80/90/100 to 60/80/100, showing how original salary plus CAO increases are used for pension accrual, while actual salary is based on the reduced percentage."], ["Compensation for disability", "Disability can be the result of an event for which someone other than the employee or employer can be held liable. In such a case, the employee must provide all information the employer needs to receive compensation for the damage suffered."], ["Death benefit", "When an employee dies, their partner receives the last earned gross salary temporarily. If there is no partner, the money goes to any minor children. The salary continues until the last day of the month following the month of death. It is usually paid out in one lump sum. Holiday pay itself is not included in the calculation. Profit-sharing payments, bonuses, expense and overtime reimbursements also do not count. Without prejudice to the provisions of article 16 of the Minimum Wage Act."], ["Working time reduction (ATV) scheme", "The weekly two hours of working time reduction do not necessarily have to be used per week. The ATV variants based on a full-time work week are: One day per week two hours off: on a fixed day or on varying days, OR two days per week one hour off: on a fixed day or on varying days, OR twelve extra days off per year, OR 24 extra half days off per year. The employer can introduce other ATV variants, but must request consent from the Works Council or personnel representation. If there is no Works Council or personnel representation, they must consult with their employee(s). For a part-time employee, there is no right to ATV because this must be incorporated into the hourly wage."], ["Vacation days entitlement", "Every employee receives vacation: free days for which their usual wages (wages in the sense of article 7:610 in conjunction with 7:639 BW) are paid. The part-time employee receives vacation days pro rata to their employment. Public holidays are separately included in the CAO, see article 3.4."], ["Accrual of vacation days", "The accrual of vacation days begins every year on 1 January. A new employee starts accruing vacation days from the moment of employment. An employee leaving the company retains the already accrued vacation days. If there is no opportunity to take those days, their value is paid out in money. If they have taken more days than they accrued, the employer may settle those excess days with the salary."], ["Extra vacation days for older employees", "From the age of 45, the employee gradually receives more vacation days. The employer may designate a maximum of five days per year as a mandatory day off (collective single day off). The remaining five days can be taken freely. Unused above-statutory vacation days expire five years after the end of the year in which they were accrued. All vacation days (both consecutive vacation and incidental single days off) are taken after consultation with the employer. The intention is for the employee to take vacation days in the year they are accrued."], ["Sickness leave policy", "In case of illness, the employee cannot (fully) work. In any case, an employee is entitled to at least 70% of their time-based wages and, for the first 52 weeks, the applicable statutory minimum wage. Childbirth of partner: statutory calamity leave. After childbirth of partner or person whose child the employee acknowledges: once the weekly working hours (so-called birth leave). Relocation: one day (per calendar year, to be determined in consultation). For taking exams for other training as referred to in article 4.2: as much time as deemed necessary by the employer. A workday normally lasts eight hours. Overtime (with extra pay) only applies if the employee works more than half an hour extra. If an employee works one hour overtime, the first 30 minutes do count. Sometimes the employment contract states that the employee always works half an hour extra. In that case, the overtime is structural. The employee then receives the overtime compensation for the first 30 minutes after the eight-hour workday. Overtime also includes all extra work outside normal working hours. Normal working hours are between 07:00 and 19:00. Anyone who has to work before 07:00 and/or after 19:00 performs overtime. They therefore receive extra pay for this."], ["General overtime rules", "The employer tries to prevent overtime. But in special circumstances - if it is unavoidable - they can oblige the employee to do so. The employee is informed in time when they have to work overtime. No one is obliged to work more than five hours per week, or more than sixteen hours per period of four weeks. Older employees (from 50 years) never have to work overtime."], ["Overtime compensation calculation", "Overtime compensation is a percentage of the normal hourly wage. The amount of that percentage is dependent on when the overtime is worked, and on the duration of the overtime."], ["Overtime rates Monday to Friday", "The first two hours of overtime: 25 percent. The hours thereafter: 50 percent. The hours between 23:00 and 05:00: 100 percent. The hours between 05:00 and the start of the usual workday: 25 percent."], ["Overtime rates Saturday", "If the employee normally works on Saturday, the same compensation rates apply as on weekdays. From 23:00 until Monday morning 05:00, they receive 100 percent compensation for overtime. Only the employee who normally does not work on Saturday receives an additional compensation: hours until 13:00: 25 percent; hours after 13:00: 50 percent; hours after 23:00: 100 percent."], ["Overtime for sales representatives", "Sales representatives do not receive separate compensation for overtime."], ["Overtime for managers", "Managers of main and branch offices who can instruct others to work overtime do not receive compensation for overtime themselves."], ["Overtime compensation: time or money", "The employee chooses how the overtime compensation is paid out, either entirely in money or entirely in time. For compensation in free time, the employee is entitled to as many free hours as the number of hours they have worked overtime. They thus receive the overtime hours in free time, and on top of that, the compensation percentage in time. They must be able to take these free hours within four weeks (after the last overtime hour worked). If this is not possible due to business circumstances, the employee will still receive the total overtime compensation in money."], ["Sunday work compensation", "Sunday is not considered a normal workday.       "Vacation Days: Full-time employees are entitled to 20 statutory vacation days and 4 above-statutory vacation days per calendar year, totaling 182.4 hours or 24 days per year. This means you accrue 1.85 vacation days or 14.03 vacation hours every 4 weeks. If not employed for the full year, vacation days are pro-rata. If no shift is scheduled, 1 vacation day equals 7.6 hours, 1 week equals 38 hours, and 4 weeks equals 152 hours. If a shift is scheduled, the vacation day is the duration of the scheduled shift. This is a standard provision and cannot be deviated from. Part-time employees' vacation entitlement depends on their working hours per wage period, accruing over all hours for which they received pay, up to a maximum of 152 hours per wage period. If a shift is scheduled, the vacation day is the duration of the scheduled shift. If no shift is scheduled, the duration of the vacation day is determined pro-rata to your working hours. If not employed for the full year, vacation days are pro-rata. On-call employees do not have the right to take vacation days but receive their vacation days paid out in money every wage period, as a 9.24% allowance on their wage over a maximum of 152 hours per wage period. This is a standard provision and cannot be deviated from. You are entitled to 1 extra vacation day for every 5 years of continuous service in the security industry. This specification must at least indicate: name of the employer and employee, the amount of the wage, the period over which the wage was earned, the composition of the wage and any allowances, and the deductions applied to the wage."
    ],
    [
      "Confidentiality",
      "The employee must keep confidential matters secret, for which confidentiality has been imposed, or of which they should reasonably understand that confidentiality is expected. This applies both during and after the employment contract."
    ],
    [
      "Transfer",
      "The employee can, in consultation – and in case of temporary transfer after consultation – for reasons of business interest, be transferred to another branch of the employer. In case of temporary transfer, this can also be a branch of an enterprise affiliated with the employer, provided it also falls under the scope of this CAO. Transfer is possible, unless it cannot reasonably be demanded of the employee."

    ],

      "The employer offers the employee a written employment contract upon commencement of employment.     ],
    [
      "Probation Period",
      "For a fixed-term employment contract of more than 6 months and for an indefinite-term employment contract, the probation period during the term of this CAO is two months. During this period, the employment contract can be terminated without further ado with immediate effect by the employer or by the employee. No dismissal permit is required and no notice period applies. For a fixed-term employment contract of 6 months or shorter, no probation period can be agreed upon."
    ],
    [
      "Chain Rule for Temporary Workers",
      "If an employer hires a former temporary worker who immediately prior worked for the employer as a temporary worker, the various temporary employment contracts are considered as one employment contract for the combined duration of the temporary employment contracts. The employee who, after having worked as a temporary worker for the employer, immediately enters into employment with the employer, therefore begins the second chain contract."

      "Employer and employee can agree on flexible deployment. In that case, the employment contract states how many hours the employee works on average per week. These are the contract hours or basic hours and serve as the starting point for flexible working."

      "If flexible working has been agreed, the employer can oblige the employee to work weekly more or fewer hours within a bandwidth of + and - 35 percent relative to the number of basic hours.     [
      "Flexible Working - Realized Hours",
      "The following types of hours are counted as realized hours (see also Article 4.2 of this CAO): all actually worked hours; paid sick leave hours; taken and paid vacation hours; taken and paid special leave; compensation of allowances in time; and other existing compensation in hours at individual enterprises. Every presence of the employee required by the employer must be considered as working time, with the exception of an incidental and not pre-planned limited exceeding of the scheduled hours. Such an incidental and/or limited exceeding does not count as realized hours and is therefore not paid."

Plus hours worked in the reference period do not automatically lead to an adjustment of the number of contract hours agreed in the individual employment contract."

The employer can in principle not refuse a request, unless there are compelling business interests, which must be demonstrated by the employer. The employer will indicate in writing as soon as possible, but no later than one month before the desired start date, whether the request is granted. If the employer has not responded within this period, the request is deemed to have been granted. For an employee with a contractual working week greater than 20 hours, the foregoing also applies, with the understanding that this concerns a maximum of 1 roster-free day per week. Saturdays and Sundays are excluded from the non-schedulable days to be agreed upon. The possibility to indicate non-schedulable days does not apply to on-call workers."

      "Change of function; retraining, re-skilling, and additional training (Article 36): An employee who will perform a function classified in a higher salary group will maintain at least their current salary. This also applies to an employee who will perform a different function classified in the same salary group. An employee who will perform a function classified in a lower salary group will continue to receive the salary earned in the previous function for at least three payment periods. Subsequently, they may be classified into the new salary group, possibly gradually. Deviating from the above, for an employee of 55 years or older classified in a lower salary group, the difference between the old and new salary will be paid as an allowance. Salary increases will only be calculated on the new salary. The allowance will remain unchanged. For an employee taken into retraining upon commencing employment, no salary scale applies during the first three payment periods. Retraining is defined as education to regain the wholly or partially lost ability to perform a specific function that the employee being trained performed. For an employee taken into re-skilling upon commencing employment, no salary scale applies during the first six payment periods, with the understanding that this term of six to twelve payment periods is extended if re-skilling takes place for a function classified in one of the salary groups higher than D. For an employee who, upon commencing employment, will receive additional training to acquire more professional knowledge, respectively skills, for performing their function, no salary scale will apply during the first three payment periods if the additional training takes place during daily working hours. An employee already in service who, during daily working hours, at the employer's request, follows a course for retraining, re-skilling, or additional training, as mentioned in lids 5 to 7, will not experience a salary reduction during the course. The employer may agree with an employee who is undergoing retraining, re-skilling, or additional training that the employment will not be terminated by either party within one year after the training has been completed, whether successfully or not. Such an agreement must be entered into in writing. Such an agreement may also stipulate that the employer will place the employee in the function for which they have been retrained, re-skilled, or additionally trained, respectively that the employee will accept the said function. An employee who terminates the employment before the time referred to in lid 9 is liable for damages. The compensation is limited to the salary, increased by any costs the employer may have incurred on behalf of the employee in connection with their participation in the course, such as books, travel expenses, etc."

Periodic Salary: Is an hourly wage (definition) laid down in the CAO or employment terms regulation (avr) of the client? If yes, the hourly wage belonging to the determined function classification must be determined based on the hourly wage or hourly wage definition as applied by the client. The irregularity or overtime surcharges are converted into time that the temporary worker can take as leave. For this temporary worker, the period of 52 worked weeks can be extended until the training is completed and up to a maximum of 104 worked weeks. When the period of 52 worked weeks is extended, the temporary worker is entitled to a second periodic increase from the 53rd week. After the expiry of the extended period of (maximum) 104 worked weeks, the temporary worker is fully remunerated according to the client's remuneration, as referred to in Article 16. The counting of 52 and 104 worked weeks referred to in lid 8 and 9 continues after an interruption of two years or less. The duration of the interruption is not included in the term of 52 and 104 worked weeks. After full utilization of the term of 52 and 104 worked weeks, the counting cannot restart. The hourly wage is adjusted by CAO parties twice a year, on January 1 and July 1, by the percentage concerning the increase of the legal minimum wage. The adjustment of the hourly wage is applied as follows: a. the salary table is increased by the agreed percentage, and b. the temporary worker's actual hourly wage is increased by the percentage concerning the increase of the legal minimum wage as of the agreed date. If the increase of the hourly wage coincides with a periodic increase, the actual hourly wage is first increased, and then the periodic increase is applied."

      "Pension scheme details (Article 32): A pension scheme has been agreed upon by CAO parties, which provides for pension accrual for temporary workers. This pension scheme is laid down in the pension agreement and is attached as an annex to this CAO. Stichting Pensioenfonds voor Personeelsdiensten (StiPP) has been entrusted by CAO parties with the execution of the pension scheme. The pension agreement is laid down in the statutes and regulations of StiPP. The pension scheme consists of a Basic Scheme and a Plus Scheme. For the rights and obligations of temporary workers and temporary employment agencies, the statutes and regulations of StiPP are decisive. CAO parties agree on the premium. The premium amounts to: a. for the Basic Scheme 8% of the pensionable salary; b. for the Plus Scheme a maximum of 12% of the pensionable salary. Of this premium, the temporary employment agency may deduct a maximum of one-third from the temporary worker's gross wage. Deviation from the Basic and Plus pension schemes as described in this agreement is always allowed in favor of the temporary worker. The regulations and further information can be found at www.stippensioen.nl."

      "Basic Scheme - Waiting period and participation: The temporary worker becomes a participant in the Basic Scheme as soon as he has completed the waiting period. During the waiting period, the temporary worker is not yet a participant and no pension is accrued. The waiting period for the Basic Scheme ends when the temporary worker has worked for more than 8 weeks for one temporary employment agency. For counting the weeks of the waiting period, referred to in lid 1, the following rules apply: a. Only weeks in which work has actually been performed are counted. The reason why no work is performed is irrelevant. b. For counting the weeks, work must have been performed for one and the same temporary employment agency, unless there is a situation as described under sub d and e. c. The worked weeks do not have to be consecutive to count, but if there is an interruption between the worked weeks of more than 26 weeks, the counting restarts. d. In case of successive employment, the relevant employment history with the previous employer is counted for the worked weeks, in accordance with Article 12 of the CAO. e. In case of a group as referred to in Article 2:24b BW, the relevant employment history with previous employers within the same group is counted for the worked weeks. f. The employer can also be an employer who has an exemption from StiPP. The temporary worker can also become a participant in the Basic Scheme if he: a. on the basis of a collective and/or individual employment agreement is entitled to earlier participation in the Basic Scheme than after completing the waiting period for the Basic Scheme (8 weeks), or; b. is no longer employed by a temporary employment agency, but has voluntarily continued his participation after termination of employment. This possibility and the rules for it are stated in the pension regulations of StiPP. For participation in the Basic Scheme, participation in the pension scheme of an employer who has an exemption from StiPP is considered equivalent. The temporary worker cannot participate in the Basic Scheme earlier than on the first day of the month in which he turns 21. If the temporary worker was a participant in the Basic Scheme and he enters into a new temporary employment agreement and: a. the interruption between the two temporary employment agreements lasts less than 52 weeks, he becomes a participant in the Basic Scheme again. b. the interruption between the two temporary employment agreements lasts 52 weeks or longer, he does not become a participant in the Basic Scheme and will have to complete the waiting period again. Transition rule waiting period: Until 2022, a waiting period of 26 weeks for the Basic Scheme was applicable. For the temporary worker who was still in the 26-week waiting period in week 1 of 2022, the following rules apply: a. The temporary worker who worked for more than 8 weeks for the same temporary employment agency in week 1 of 2022, becomes a participant in the Basic Scheme as of week 1 of 2022. b. If the temporary worker had not yet worked 8 weeks for the same temporary employment agency in week 1 of 2022, the weeks worked before week 1 of 2022 count towards the waiting period. The aforementioned week 1 of 2022, starting on January 3, 2022, applies to employers who pay wages weekly or every 4 weeks. For employers who pay wages monthly, the aforementioned week 1 applies as January 1, 2022. For the week counting in this transition rule, the same rules apply as for the waiting period described in lid 2. Stichting Pensioenfonds voor Personeelsdiensten is entrusted with the execution of the Basic Scheme. CAO parties involved in the ABU and NBBU CAOs have agreed that the average premium for weekly wage payment as of January 2, 2023, and for monthly wage payment as of January 1, 2023, amounts to 8% of the pensionable salary. The pensionable salary is the pensionable wage, reduced by the franchise. The pensionable salary cannot be less than zero. The franchise per period is determined by multiplying the number of paid hours in the relevant period by the hourly franchise. The hourly franchise is determined annually by the board of StiPP and is derived from the annual franchise which is equal to the amount taken as a starting point in Article 10aa, lid 1, of the Uitvoeringsbesluit loonbelasting 1965 for an accrual percentage of 1.788% and a 36-hour work week. The pensionable wage per period of a week, four weeks, or a calendar month in the sense of this article consists of the sum of: the wage for employee insurance. The addition due to private use of a company car is always excluded from this; the employee's share in the premium for the pension scheme; the wage that has been exchanged for tax-free reimbursements or tax-free provisions in connection with extraterritorial costs. The pensionable wage is pensionable up to a maximum hourly amount. This maximum hourly amount is determined annually by the board of StiPP and is derived from the maximum insured amount for social insurance as described in Chapter 3 of the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen. Transition rule reservations: If the temporary worker was already a participant in the StiPP pension scheme before January 1, 2022, and the reservations were included in the pensionable wage/gross hourly wage at the time of accrual in accordance with the regulations applicable in the relevant year, these reservations will be deducted from the pensionable wage from 2022 to prevent double pension accrual over the same part of the wage. The full Basic Scheme is laid down in the Basic Scheme regulations of Stichting Pensioenfonds voor Personeelsdiensten."

If it is not clear from the temporary employment agreement or the assignment whether the public holiday falls on a day that would normally be considered his working day, the temporary worker is granted a public holiday if: a. the temporary worker has worked at least seven times on the relevant day of the week in a period of thirteen consecutive weeks immediately preceding the public holiday; or b. the temporary worker has not yet worked thirteen consecutive weeks and has worked on the relevant day of the week in more than half of the weeks worked. Temporary employment agreement with temporary employment clause: If the temporary worker is entitled to a public holiday, the following applies regarding wage payment.
